title: Breastfeeding Basics
learningGoal: Help parents understand the fundamentals of breastfeeding, including positioning, attachment, and recognising feeding cues.
microLesson: Breastfeeding supports nutrition, bonding, and emotional security. Many early challenges come from positioning or attachment issues rather than milk supply. Watching for early feeding cues—such as rooting, hand-to-mouth movements, or restlessness—helps prevent distress. A calm environment, skin-to-skin contact, and responsive feeding support success. Parents should seek help early if feeding becomes painful or stressful; support makes a significant difference.
activity: Identify two early feeding cues your baby shows. During one feeding session, respond to those cues and write a reflection on how your baby reacted.
